specification_compliance: All six findings are about touch-point scope, not behaviour. Each new or edited file they name exists at the commit and is referenced as the finding describes.

Five new modules sit outside the touch-point list: useMergedCollectionOrder.ts, useSmartCollectionActions.ts, useNameSubmission.ts, nameInUse.ts and apiError.ts. ConfirmDialog.tsx is also edited outside the list. The spec's touch-point list does not cover any of these, so it is out of date or incomplete. Whether that matters depends on the spec's own scope rule, which I did not check.
potential_unspecified_behavior: ConfirmDialog now portals to document.body. Callers rendered inside transformed or stacking-context ancestors will now draw above their own containers, which is the intended effect of the Sidebar fix commit but was not in the spec. I did not check each caller for a visual change.
regression_risks: The ConfirmDialog portal changes every caller, and the frontend unit tests mock the dialog in most of them, so a regression in the real dialog's layout or focus would not show in unit tests.

Moving ApiStatusError to apiError.ts keeps the api.ts re-export, so existing imports are unaffected. A test that mocks lib/api wholesale would not replace the class, which is the intent noted in apiError.ts:4-5.
test_coverage: I did not run any tests (only Read, Glob and Grep were available). The FileContextMenu test was edited to use a portal-based stub, which I read at lines 292-307. The rest of the test coverage was not assessed.
not_verified: I did not run git, so I could not check that the worktree matches commit 641156b8f or see the diff. The claim that ConfirmDialog.tsx was changed in this commit rests on classification.json, not on the diff.
I did not verify whether any caller of ConfirmDialog changes visually or in focus behaviour under the portal.
I did not check the spec's scope rule that decides whether files outside the touch-point list are a defect, and I did not check invariants I1 to I10 against the code.
I did not run unit or e2e tests.
